questions.title: Time complexity of binary search
questions.body: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a **sorted** array of *n* elements?
questions.explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining range, so at most ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 comparisons are needed.

questions.title: Average lookup cost in a hash map
questions.body: Assuming a good hash function and a bounded load factor, what is the **average** time to look up a key in a hash map?
questions.explanation: With keys spread evenly across buckets, each bucket holds O(1) entries on average. The worst case degrades to O(n) when many keys collide.

questions.title: Detecting a cycle with constant extra space
questions.body: Which technique detects a cycle in a singly linked list using **O(1)** extra memory?
questions.explanation: Floyd's algorithm moves a slow pointer one step and a fast pointer two steps; they meet if and only if there is a cycle.

options.text: Store visited nodes in a hash set
Fast and slow pointers (Floyd's cycle detection)
Reverse the list and compare with the original
Sort the node addresses and look for duplicates

questions.title: Traversal that lists a BST in sorted order
questions.body: Which depth-first traversal of a **binary search tree** visits its keys in ascending order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal visits the left subtree, then the node, then the right subtree, which is exactly ascending order for a BST.

questions.title: When dynamic programming applies
questions.body: Which properties make a problem a good fit for dynamic programming? **Select all that apply.**
questions.explanation: DP needs optimal substructure (optimal answers built from optimal sub-answers) and overlapping subproblems (the same subproblems recur, so caching pays off).

options.text: A greedy choice is always safe

questions.title: JOIN that keeps only matching rows
questions.body: Which SQL join returns **only** the rows that have matching values in both tables?
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN keeps only matched pairs. LEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER joins also keep unmatched rows from one or both sides, filled with NULLs.

questions.title: Which is not a deadlock condition?
questions.body: Deadlock can only occur when four conditions hold at once. Which of these is **not** one of them?
questions.explanation: The four (Coffman) conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Preemptive scheduling is unrelated.

questions.title: Meaning of HTTP 404
questions.body: A server responds to a request with status code **404**. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 404 Not Found means the server has no resource at that URL. 401/403 concern authentication/authorisation, and 5xx codes are server errors.

options.text: The server crashed while handling the request

questions.title: Pair with target sum
questions.body:
Given an array of integers and a target, print the **0-based indices** of the two numbers that add up to the target (smaller index first). Exactly one answer exists.

**Input**
- Line 1: `n` and `target`
- Line 2: `n` space-separated integers

**Output**
- Two indices separated by a space
questions.explanation: Scan once, storing each value's index in a hash map; for each element check whether `target - value` was seen. O(n) time, O(n) space.

starterCode.python:
n, target = map(int, input().split())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# print the two indices

questions.title: Balanced brackets
questions.body:
A string contains only the characters `()[]{}`. Print `true` if every bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order, otherwise `false`.

**Input**: one line containing the string (may be empty).
questions.explanation: Push opening brackets on a stack; on a closing bracket the top must be its partner. The string is balanced if the stack ends empty.

starterCode.python:
s = input().strip()
# print true or false

questions.title: Ways to climb a staircase
questions.body: You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Print the number of distinct ways to reach the top of a staircase with `n` steps (1 ≤ n ≤ 45).
questions.explanation: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2) with ways(1)=1, ways(2)=2: a Fibonacci recurrence solved bottom-up in O(n).

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
# print the number of ways

questions.title: Maximum subarray sum
questions.body:
Print the largest sum of any **non-empty contiguous** subarray.

**Input**
- Line 1: `n`
- Line 2: `n` space-separated integers
questions.explanation: Kadane's algorithm: keep the best sum ending at the current index (max(x, best + x)) and the best seen overall. O(n) time, O(1) space.

starterCode.python:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
# print the maximum subarray sum
